Subject: RFI — DR procedures and PII handling for on-prem/private deployment

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. As part of our security board's RFI, we need a consolidated response that covers disaster recovery procedures, recovery time objectives, and the data flow for sensitive PHI/PII in a private (VPC/on-prem/air-gapped) deployment. Specific asks:

- Primary/secondary site failover steps and expected RTO/RPO for operator-managed on-prem clusters.
- How KV cache and model weights are protected at-rest and during transfer (if any transfer is allowed).
- Operator access controls, emergency access (break-glass) procedures, and audit log retention.
- Any tooling or runbooks you provide for practice DR drills and operator failover testing.
- A simple network diagram showing ingress/egress controls and where telemetry/metrics live.

Can you send a single ZIP or pack with the above artifacts and a short statement we can circulate to our board? Procurement would like a rough timeline to close the procurement SOW, too.

Appreciate it,
Jorge

--
Jorge Silva
Head of IT Security, Clearsight Health
From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai

Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFI — DR procedures and PII handling for on-prem/private deployment

Jorge — thanks, clear list. I can get a consolidated pack together by next Tuesday. Quick notes in-line:

- RTO/RPO: Standard private deployment baseline is RTO = 4 hours (hot standby within same region) and RPO = 15 minutes with operator-managed async replication. For customers needing sub-hour RTO we'll propose a dedicated cross-site replication add-on.
- KV cache & weights: All persisted artifacts (weights, config snapshots) are encrypted with customer KMS/HSM keys; in-air transfers are TLS 1.3 with mTLS. Runtime KV caches are ephemeral and never persisted to disk unless configured for warm-restart (in which case they're encrypted).
- Operator access: Role-based access (RBAC) + short-lived certificates. Emergency break-glass requires two-person approval and generates a signed audit event.
- DR drills: we provide a runbook and a test harness that can be run during maintenance windows; afterwards Redwood provides a drill report template.
- Network diagram: attaching a simplified diagram and a draft DR plan for your board.

Attachments (for review): redwood_dr_plan_v1.pdf, private-deploy-network-diagram.png

I'll loop in Ben for the operator matrix and Rishi for the cryptography/KEK notes. Expect a consolidated zip and short executive summary by Tue 06 Oct. Do you need a separate SOW timeline for procurement earlier than that?

Best,
Laura Bennett
Enterprise Sales Lead — Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 08:24:00 -0700
Subject: operator access matrix + maintenance windows (Clearsight RFI)

Jorge / team — adding the operator perspective. Key clarifications and items we'll include in the pack:

1) Operator access matrix (attached) — maps roles (Operator, SRE, Customer Admin) to allowed actions (deploy, rollback, keystore rotation, emergency shell). The operator role is scoped per-customer and isolated in the orchestration plane.
2) Break-glass flow — documented approval chain + automatic session recordings.
3) Maintenance windows — Default: weekly 2hr window for patching; emergency patching requires 24h notice except critical CVEs.
4) Telemetry & logs — telemetry is configurable; PII is redacted at the collector before leaving the air-gapped boundary. For customers requiring zero egress, telemetry collectors can be run in a local-only mode; we will slot an operator-run export process for audits.

Attachment: operator-access-matrix.xlsx

I recommend one follow-up 30-minute call with your compliance folks so we can walk the kid-glove scenarios (air-gap + limited egress). Laura — happy to run that with Vanessa.

-ben

Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: RFI — DR procedures and PII handling for on-prem/private deployment

Hi Jorge — Vanessa here from Deployments/Customer Ops. A few operational details to set expectations before the board:

- Operator training: we provide an initial 3-day on-site (or remote) operator training and a 6-week runbook handover window.
- Patch/upgrade process: upgrades are staged in a sandbox cluster first; operator sign-off required for production promotion.
- Incident telemetries: audit logs retained for 1 year by default, can be extended; exportable as CSV for audits.
- DR test cadence: recommended twice-yearly full DR drills; we can run the first one with your team and produce an after-action report.

I'll include suggested language for your board summary in the pack. Also, Laura — procurement asked about an expedited SOW timeline. We can deliver the signed SOW + initial onboarding within 3 weeks from contract signature for standard private deployments.

Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Deployments, Redwood Inference
